Fly the aircraft

Vector sticks

Pick an aircraft, press Draw, then click points on the map. Drag the white handle in the middle of a stick to curve it. Pull it back to the middle to make it straight. Drag an end point to move it. Tap a point you already drew to stack another point on it. Click a Jack to get the option to commit: the aircraft slows, stops there for the time you set, then flies on. Flown sticks clear off the map. Press Play to fly it. Before you click, small text by the cursor shows the distance to the nearest threat.

Pressure altitude and OAT set how fast the aircraft speeds up. Pick a chart line above to use them for turn rate too.

Before you first press Play, a heading you enter points the aircraft that way at once, as its starting position. After that it turns to the heading. Setting a heading or turn by hand cancels that aircraft's pattern or sticks.

Formation

In ground track mode, trail flies the same path lead flew and holds the spacing above, measured along the track it is about to fly. Editing trail on its own takes it out of formation. Tick the box again to rejoin.

The pattern starts where the aircraft is now and repeats. With sticks drawn, it goes on the end of the last stick.

On the map, drag the pattern's line or middle handle to move it, and the amber handle to rotate it. The aircraft joins at the nearest point.

Leave turn time blank to size turns from the turn rate. Seconds use the airspeed when you press Fly, with no wind. A circle sets the aircraft to the airspeed you enter.

Flex fire guns

Use the GUNS bar on the map. Tap L or R to turn a gun on. Each gun has its own target picker next to it. A gun that is on shoots only while it is clear to shoot. It stops by itself when it is not, and starts again when it is.

Guns also have up and down stops. The sim uses your height above the target and the bank angle to work out how far up or down the gun must point, and holds fire when that is past a stop. Banking toward the target lifts it against the upper stop. Each gun is checked by itself against its own gun target line. A gun is clear when its target is inside its arc and range, no Jack is within 30° of its line, and the other aircraft is far enough off its line. The other aircraft and a Jack only count when they are inside that gun's own arc, since the gun cannot swing past its stops. The spacing needed is 2 clock positions (60°) when the other aircraft is hot, which means closing on the line, and 1 clock position (30°) when it is cold.

The arc is 90° forward and 81° aft of straight out the side, which is the nose back to 171°. The forward limit starts at 1° off the nose, so neither gun shoots straight ahead. Set it to 0 to let both guns shoot on the nose. Max range is a placeholder. Set it to what you want to train to.

Map image

Pick a built-in map. It comes in with north up and its scale already set, with lead at the map's start point. Or load your own screenshot of a map or satellite view. You can also paste a copied screenshot with Ctrl+V. Then set its scale so distances are true.

Set the scale: press Draw scale line, drag between two points on the image that you know the distance between (the map's own scale bar works well), type that distance, and press Apply.

Custom terrain

Pick a type, press Draw terrain, then drag on the map to trace the outline. Let go and the shape fills in. To remove one shape, pick the Erase tool and click it.

Save and load

Saved setups

A setup keeps the background, map image, terrain, wind, chart turn rate choice, threats, Jacks, both aircraft (position, heading, airspeed), spacing, sticks, and patterns as they are right now.

Nothing saved yet

Setups are kept in this browser on this device. To move one to another device or keep a backup, copy its code and paste it there. A code does not carry the map image, so load the picture again on the other device.

Saved recordings

Press ● Record on the map, fly, then press Stop. Name it here and press Save. A saved recording keeps both aircraft, the threats, Jacks, terrain and background. It does not keep the map image.

Nothing saved yet

Recordings are kept in this browser on this device. Saving with a name you already used replaces the old one.

↶ Undo on the map takes back your last action and puts the sim back to the moment just before it, and ↷ Redo puts it back. ● Record saves what the aircraft do until you press Stop. Play recording then replays it with the ground tracks and without sticks or patterns. Use the slider to jump around, and Exit playback to return to where you were. + Pattern in the Map tool bar lets you pick a pattern type and adds it, using the sizes set in the Gunnery pattern box. On a touch screen, pinch to zoom and drag with two fingers to move the map. Hide controls gives the map the whole screen and puts the map tools on its left edge. There, ☰ All tools opens any section of the controls right on the map. Keys: 7 8 9 0 1 2 set 70 to 120 kt, − and = change airspeed by 5, M move map, S sticks, R measure, E erase, T trail follows lead, Esc closes a section. Use ◀ 1 s and 1 s ▶ on the map to step back or forward one second at a time. The Left and Right arrow keys do the same, and Space plays or pauses. You can go back up to 10 minutes.

You can drag aircraft, threats, Jacks, and patterns in every tool except Measure and Terrain.

Wind pushes the aircraft. On sticks or a pattern they crab into the wind to hold the line. Aircraft in formation are drawn larger than scale when zoomed out.
